setting.placeName:
Legation of the United States,
Republic of Liberia, Monrovia

opener.dateline:
Legation of the United States,
Republic of Liberia, Monrovia, June 6, 1874.

div.p: Sir: In compliance with my promise, I have the honor to transmit herewith, for your information and guidance, copies of correspondence that has taken place between this legation and the government of Liberia in reference to a national salute and the President’s formal reception of yourself this day.

list.label: 1st.
list.item: I will arrive on board in person at 9.30 a.m.
list.label: 2d.
list.item: The salute will commence at 12 o’clock noon.
list.label: 3d.
list.item: His excellency has appointed 11 o’clock for the reception of yourself and officers at the executive mansion, at the conclusion of which reception I anticipate the happiness of being able to submit to your consideration such courtesy as others have seen fit to extend to you on your visit.

div.p: I shall be happy to render you such service as you may require and that shall be found to be within my official province. Should such service be required, you will be good enough to send by the bearer of this dispatch a written description of the same.
I sincerely regret to have been informed by your officer on shore yesterday of your indisposition. I hope, however, you are better to-day.

My congratulations to yourself, officers, and men. Wishing you all bon voyage, I have the happinesss to pray you to accept, my dear captain, my sincere assurances of the high consideration and esteem with which I have the distinguished honor to be, sir,

list.item:
Capt. Earl English,
Commanding United States Ship Congress, off Monrovia.
